resources.string: The BRDM-2 is a Russian reconnaissance armored vehicle. It was developed in the Soviet Union in the early 1950s. The BRDM-2 entered service in 1962. Its armament consists of the 14.5mm KPVT heavy machine gun and the 7.62mm PKT coaxial machine gun, identical to the Russian BTR-60/BTR-70/BTR-80 armored personnel carriers. The BRDM-2, in different versions, is used by the armed forces of more than 50 countries worldwide. Crew: 4

The ATF Dingo is a German-produced armored military vehicle. The standard armament of the Dingo is a 7.62mm machine gun turret. It can be replaced with a 12.7mm machine gun or an HK GMG automatic grenade launcher.
The Eagle V is a Swiss 4×4 wheeled multi-role armored vehicle. It was developed in the 2010s by GDELS-Mowag, General Dynamics European Land Systems-Mowag. The Eagle V entered service in 2015.

The Komatsu LAV, Light Armored Vehicle, is a Japanese 4×4 wheeled light armored vehicle. It was developed in the 1990s. The Komatsu LAV entered service in 2001. It is optimized for reconnaissance and patrol missions. The vehicle hull is protected against 7.62mm ammunition. The vehicle can receive a 12.7mm heavy machine gun or a 7.62mm machine gun on the superstructure. The anti-tank version is equipped with Type 87 or Type 01 LMAT missiles. Crew: 4 + 1.

The VBMR-L (Light Multi-Role Armored Vehicles) Serval is a French 4×4 wheeled armored vehicle. It was developed by Nexter Systems and Texelis. The VBMR-L Serval entered service in 2022. It will be developed in several versions: Troop transport, Command post, Artillery observation, Engineer vehicle, Medical evacuation, SA2R, Tactical communication group, etc. The VBMR-L Serval is equipped with communication means and the SCORPION combat information system (SICS). Armament: 12.7mm machine gun. Crew: 2 + 8.

The GAZ-2330 Tigr is a Russian 4×4 wheeled armored vehicle. It was developed in the early 2000s. The Tigr entered service in 2006. The GAZ-2330 Tigr is a multi-role armored vehicle. It is used for troop transport, patrol, reconnaissance, and equipment carrying missions. No organic armament. Crew: 2 + 7.

The Vamtac is a Spanish 4×4 wheeled light armored vehicle. It was developed in the 1980s-1990s by URO Vehiculos Especiales. The Vamtac entered service in 1998. The Vamtac is exported to Saudi Arabia, Dominican Republic, Ghana, Indonesia, Iraq, Malaysia, Morocco, Portugal, Romania and Singapore. It is also marketed in its civilian version.

The VBL, Light Armored Vehicle, is a French 4×4 wheeled light armored vehicle. It was developed in the 1980s. The VBL entered service in 1990. The VBL is particularly suited for reconnaissance missions due to its reduced dimensions and noise level. The basic version has a crew of three: driver, crew commander and scout. The VBL can integrate different weapon systems: 7.62mm machine gun on a ring mount, 12.7mm machine gun in a turret, 40mm automatic grenade launcher, MILAN or TOW anti-tank missiles. The VBL has amphibious capability and is propelled in water by a propeller.

The Fennek is a German 4×4 wheeled armored vehicle. It was developed in the 1990s. The Fennek entered service in 2003. The Fennek has the driver\'s position in the center at the front of the vehicle and two crew members are placed side by side in the central part. The powertrain is located at the rear of the vehicle. The reconnaissance version is equipped with a retractable optical module. Different models are developed for reconnaissance, anti-tank, engineer, air defense, and artillery observation units. Armament: 7.62mm / 12.7mm / 40mm automatic grenade launcher. Crew: 3.

Unveiled to the general public for the first time during the July 14, 2023 national celebration. Designed for reconnaissance and intervention missions for French special forces. The Grizzly is equipped with a circular turret capable of receiving heavy weapons, such as the M2HB in 12.7mm caliber or the AGL in 40mm caliber, as well as three 7.62mm machine gun mounts.

The HMMWV, High Mobility Multipurpose Wheeled Vehicle, is a family of American 4×4 wheeled vehicles. It was developed in the 1980s. The HMMWV entered service in 1984. The HMMWV is more commonly called Humvee. It is very widely distributed worldwide. From 2018, the HMMWV begins to be replaced by the MRAP category JLTV armored vehicle.
The TPz1 Fuchs is a German 6×6 wheeled armored personnel carrier. It was developed in the late 1970s. Armament: 7.62mm machine gun. Crew: 2 + 8.

The Piranha V infantry fighting vehicle (IFV) is the fifth generation variant of the Mowag Piranha vehicle family. Place of origin: Switzerland. The Piranha V entered service in 2015. Used by: Denmark / Monaco / Spain / Romania.

The BMR-600 is a Spanish 6×6 wheeled armored personnel carrier. It was developed in the 1970s. The BMR-600 entered service in 1979. Nearly 1,500 BMR-600s have been produced in different versions. It has been exported to Egypt, Saudi Arabia and Peru. Armament: 12.7mm, M2HB. Crew: 3 + 8.

The Wiesel is a German reconnaissance armored vehicle. It was developed in the 1980s. The Wiesel entered service in 1989. The Wiesel is developed in two main versions: the Wiesel 1 Mk 20 armed with a Mk 20 Rh 202 20mm dual-feed automatic cannon for reconnaissance and fire support missions and the Wiesel 1 TOW for anti-tank combat. Crew: 2 – Wiesel Mk20 / 3 – Wiesel TOW.

The VBM Freccia, Veicolo Blindato Medio, is an Italian 8×8 wheeled infantry fighting vehicle. It was developed in the 2000s. The Freccia entered service in 2008. The Freccia chassis is developed from the Italian B1 Centauro light tank chassis. The Freccia is equipped with a HITFIST 25 Plus two-man turret armed with a 25mm Oerlikon KBA cannon. The armament is complemented by two 7.62mm machine guns and the capability to receive Spike anti-tank missiles. Crew: 3 + 8.

The XA-180 is a Finnish 6×6 wheeled armored personnel carrier. It was developed in the 1980s. The XA-180 entered service in 1984. The XA-180 is also known as Pasi, Panssari Sisu – Armored Sisu in Finnish. It was developed at the request of the Finnish army to replace the Soviet BTR-60 armored personnel carriers. The XA-180 is developed in several versions and exported to the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden, Ireland and Estonia. Armament: 12.7mm or 7.62mm. Crew: 2 + 10 to 16.
Pandur II: armored personnel carrier originating from Austria.

The Cobra is a Turkish 4×4 wheeled combat armored vehicle. It was developed in the 1990s. The Cobra is employed by the armed forces of Turkey, Georgia, Azerbaijan, Pakistan, Algeria, Bahrain, United Arab Emirates, Kazakhstan, Kosovo, Nigeria, Bangladesh, Macedonia, Montenegro and Slovenia.
The Ulan is an Austrian infantry fighting vehicle. It was developed in the early 1990s. The Ulan entered service in 2001. Cannon: 30mm, Mauser MK 30/2. Coaxial machine gun: 7.62mm. Crew: 3 + 8.

The Pizarro is a Spanish infantry fighting vehicle. It was developed in the early 1990s. The Pizarro entered service in 2001. The Pizarro was developed as part of the ASCOD program, Austrian Spanish Cooperation Development, of the future infantry fighting vehicle for the Austrian and Spanish armed forces. The Austrian version, named Ulan, has several differences. Cannon: 30mm. Coaxial machine gun: 7.62mm. Crew: 3 + 8.

The PTL-02 is a Chinese heavy weapons vehicle. It was developed in the 1990s – early 2000s. The PTL-02 entered service in 2012. The PTL-02 was developed to provide infantry units with fire support. It uses the reinforced chassis of the WZ-551 6×6 wheeled armored personnel carrier. The main armament consists of the 100mm cannon. The ammunition load is 30 shells. Crew: 4 + 1.

The B1 Centauro is an Italian 8×8 wheeled light tank. It was developed in the 1980s by the Iveco – Fiat consortium. The B1 Centauro entered service in 1991. The B1 Centauro is intended for reconnaissance units. The rear of the chassis has a door to facilitate access on board and ammunition loading. In addition to its crew, four infantrymen can take place at the rear of the vehicle on folding seats, in place of part of the ammunition stock. The B1 Centauro is armed with a 105mm stabilized, manually loaded cannon. The B1 Centauro chassis gave birth to the VBM Freccia infantry vehicle.

The AAV, Assault Amphibious Vehicle, is an American amphibious armored personnel carrier. It was developed in the 1970s. The AAV entered service in 1972 under the name LVTP-7. Machine gun: M2HB 12.7mm. Automatic grenade launcher: Mk19 40mm. Crew: 3 + 21.

The Achzarit is an Israeli heavy armored personnel carrier. It was developed in the 1980s from the T-55 battle tank chassis. The Achzarit entered service in 1988. The Achzarit Mk II entered service in 1997. It has the new 850 hp engine and reinforced running gear with new road wheels, sprockets and tracks. Machine gun: 7.62mm MAG-58 remotely operated or 12.7mm remotely operated. Crew: 3 + 7.

The HMT 400 is a modular armored vehicle. It is developed by Supacat from the ATMP chassis in 4×4 HMT 400, 6×6 HMT 600 and 6×6 HMT Extenda Mk2 versions. The Jackal carries three crew members and can be employed for reconnaissance missions. It has a high level of mine protection and can receive an additional armor kit. The armament consists of a 12.7mm heavy machine gun or an automatic grenade launcher and a 7.62mm machine gun.

The ZTD-05 is a Chinese Heavy Weapons Vehicle. It was developed in the late 1990s. The ZTD-05 entered service in 2005. The ZTD-05 uses the chassis of the Chinese ZBD-05 amphibious infantry fighting vehicle, also called Type-05. The ZBD-ZTD vehicle family developed for marine infantry units is optimized for landing missions. It is equipped with a two-man turret armed with a stabilized 105mm cannon. It can fire while moving on land and water. Crew: 4.

The BMO-T is a Russian heavy armored personnel carrier. It was developed in the 1990s from the T-72 battle tank chassis. The BMO-T entered service in 2001 in limited quantities. Russia is the only user of the BMO-T. Machine gun: 12.7mm. Rocket launcher: 30 PRO-A Shmel thermobaric effect. Crew: 2 + 7.

The M1126 Stryker is an American 8×8 wheeled armored personnel carrier. It was developed in the late 1990s. The M1126 Stryker entered service in 2002. The M1126 Stryker is developed from the Canadian LAV-III Kodiak based on the Piranha III armored vehicle mechanics. It has the M151 Protector remotely operated weapon station which can receive an M2HB 12.7mm heavy machine gun or a Mk 19 40mm automatic grenade launcher. Crew: 2 + 9.

The Namer is an Israeli heavy armored personnel carrier. It was developed in the 2000s. The Namer entered service in 2008. The Namer is developed from the Merkava Mk IV battle tank chassis. Its armament consists of 12.7mm and/or 7.62mm machine guns. In July 2017, the Namer was unveiled in heavy IFV (Infantry Fighting Vehicle) version. It is equipped with a remotely operated turret, armed with a 30mm automatic cannon. Machine gun: 12.7mm. Crew: 3 + 8.

The M2 Bradley is an American infantry fighting vehicle. It was developed in the 1970s. The M2 Bradley entered service in 1981. The M2 Bradley is armed with a 25mm Bushmaster cannon. From 1986, the M1A1 model receives two TOW anti-tank missiles. The M2 Bradley has undergone several modernization campaigns improving its combat capabilities, protection level, mobility and various equipment. The M2A3 model integrates Battlefield Digitization equipment. From the M2 Bradley, a reconnaissance version was developed under the name M3 Bradley. Crew: 3 + 7.

The SPz Marder is a German infantry fighting vehicle. It was developed in the 1960s. The SPz Marder entered service in 1971. The SPz Marder is equipped with a two-man turret on the superstructure armed with a 20mm Rh 202 automatic cannon and a 7.62mm MG3A1 machine gun. The SPz Marder has been delivered to Indonesia, Jordan and Chile. Within the German armed forces, the SPz Marder is being replaced by the new SPz Puma infantry fighting vehicle. Crew: 3 + 6 to 7.

The SPz Puma is a German heavy infantry fighting vehicle. It was developed in the 2000s. The SPz Puma was developed to replace the SPz Marder in German mechanized infantry units. The SPz Puma is equipped with a remotely operated turret armed with a 30mm MK.30-2 cannon and a 5.56mm coaxial machine gun. It has two protection levels. Level A, Air-transportable, with complete mine protection and ballistic protection against 30mm ammunition from the front and 14.5mm laterally. The SPz Puma level A version remains air-transportable by A-400M transport aircraft. Crew: 3 + 6.

The M113 is an American armored personnel carrier. It was developed in the 1950s. The M113 entered service in 1960. The M113 was developed for infantry units for missions of transporting a group of infantrymen. It has undergone several modernization campaigns. The M113 is derived into a wide range of specialized vehicles: command post, mortar, medical, air defense, engineer vehicle, anti-tank missile launcher, etc. It has been adopted by numerous armed forces worldwide. Machine gun: 12.7mm. Crew: 2 + 11.

The Boxer is a German 8×8 wheeled combat armored vehicle. It was developed in the 2000s. The Boxer entered service in 2009. The Boxer has a modular structure. The chassis, with the engine compartment and driver\'s position, can receive different specialized modules. The Boxer is offered for export with different equipment configurations and weapon systems. They replace part of the M113 and Fuchs TPz 1 vehicle fleet. The Boxer is put into service by Lithuania under the designation Vilkas, by Australia with licensed production and by the United Kingdom. Machine gun: 7.62mm / 12.7mm. / AGL: 40mm. Crew: 3 + 8.

The BMP-1 is a Russian infantry fighting vehicle. It was developed in the Soviet Union in the early 1960s. The BMP-1 entered service in 1966. The BMP-1, Boyevaya Machina Pekhoty – infantry fighting vehicle, is the first armored vehicle of its category. It was developed to strengthen the capabilities of mechanized infantry units. The BMP-1 is an amphibious vehicle capable of fighting in NBC environment. Its crew consists of the vehicle commander, gunner, driver and eight infantrymen. The BMP-1 is equipped with a single-man turret armed with a 73mm 2A28 Grom smoothbore cannon, a 7.62mm PKTM coaxial machine gun and the 9M14M Malyutka anti-tank missile, AT-3 Sagger. The infantrymen have the ability to fire from inside the vehicle through nine firing ports. Between 1966 and 1988, more than 20,000 BMP-1s were built. In August 2018, a new version of the BMP-1 was presented under the name BMP-1AM Basurman.

The BMP-2 is a Russian infantry fighting vehicle. It was developed in the Soviet Union in the 1970s. The BMP-2 entered service in 1981. The BMP-2 is developed based on the BMP-1 infantry fighting vehicle chassis. The powertrain is at the front right and the driver\'s position at the front left. It is amphibious and NBC protected. To improve its firepower, the BMP-2 receives a two-man turret, armed with a 30mm 2A42 automatic cannon, a 7.62mm PKT coaxial machine gun and anti-tank missiles. The BMP-2 is adopted by many armies worldwide. Crew: 3 + 7.

The BMP-3 is a Russian infantry fighting vehicle. It was developed in the Soviet Union in the 1980s. The BMP-3 entered service in 1987. The BMP-3 is the most heavily armed vehicle of its category. Its armament consists of the 100mm 2A70 low-pressure cannon, the 30mm 2A72 automatic cannon, the 7.62mm PKT coaxial machine gun. The BMP-3 can fire through the 100mm cannon the 9M117 anti-tank missile of the 9K166-3 Basnya system, AT-12 Swinger. The BMP-3 chassis adopts the configuration of the Russian airborne combat armored vehicle family BMD. Crew: 3 + 7.

The BRDM-2 is a Russian reconnaissance armored vehicle. It was developed in the Soviet Union in the early 1950s. The BRDM-2 entered service in 1962. Its armament consists of the 14.5mm KPVT heavy machine gun and the 7.62mm PKT coaxial machine gun, identical to the Russian BTR-60/BTR-70/BTR-80 armored personnel carriers. The BRDM-2, in different versions, is used by the armed forces of more than 50 countries worldwide. Crew: 4.

The BTR-60 is a Russian 8×8 wheeled armored personnel carrier. It was developed in the Soviet Union in the early 1950s. The BTR-60 entered service in 1960. The BTR-60P open-top version carries two crew members and 12 to 14 infantrymen. The armament consists of a manually operated 12.7mm machine gun and one or more 7.62mm machine guns installed on the sides. The BTR-60PA version receives a roof and benefits from NBC protection. The BTR-60PB version is equipped with a single-man turret armed with the 14.5mm KPVT heavy machine gun and the 7.62mm PKT coaxial machine gun. The BTR-60PB carries three crew members and 8 infantrymen. The BTR-60, in different versions, is very widely exported worldwide. Within the Soviet army, then Russian, the BTR-60 is replaced from 1976 by the BTR-70.

The BTR-80 is a Russian 8×8 wheeled armored personnel carrier. It was developed in the Soviet Union in the early 1980s. The BTR-80 entered service in 1986. The BTR-80 has the same architecture as its predecessor the BTR-70, with the engine at the rear of the vehicle. Access on board is through double side doors. Machine gun: 14.5mm. Coaxial machine gun: 7.62mm. Crew: 3 + 7.

The BTR-70 is a Russian 8×8 wheeled armored personnel carrier. It was developed in the Soviet Union in the early 1970s. The BTR-70 entered service in 1976. The BTR-70 has the same architecture as its predecessor the BTR-60. The BTR-70 version is equipped with a single-man turret armed with the 14.5mm KPVT heavy machine gun and the 7.62mm PKT coaxial machine gun. Crew: 3 + 7.

The BTR-80A 8x8 armored personnel carrier is designed and manufactured by Russia. It is intended for transporting troops on the battlefield and providing close fire support. It can also conduct reconnaissance, combat support and patrol missions. The first five BTR-80A vehicles were delivered to the Main Directorate of Presidential Security, based in Moscow, and were first publicly presented in May 1995. The BTR-80A is practically identical to the BTR-80, but it is equipped with a new single-man turret armed with a 30mm 2A72 cannon and a 7.62mm PKTM machine gun. Crew: 3 + 7.

The JLTV, Joint Light Tactical Vehicle, is an American 4×4 wheeled armored vehicle. It was developed in the 2010s, as part of the HMMWV replacement program. The JLTV entered service in 2018. The JLTV is developed from the L-ATV, Light Combat Tactical All-Terrain Vehicle armored wheeled vehicle. It has the ballistic protection level and mine protection of an MRAP, Mine Resistant Ambush Protected level. The vehicle can receive different types of armament with remotely operated turrets. The JLTV is actively promoted for export. Armament: 12.7mm to 20mm. Crew: 2 + 2 to 3.
An MRAP type armored personnel carrier with a V-shaped hull. Country: United States. Period of use: 2007 to present. Crew: up to 10 people. Capability to install all known combat modules.

The Casspir is a troop transport vehicle created for the South African police and armed forces in the 1970s. It is distinguished by a wide wheelbase and reinforced floor to withstand mines. It has a roof-mounted 7.62mm machine gun, but armament is often significantly increased in the field by units using the vehicles. To protect the vehicle against mines, the lower part of the hull is raised, reinforced and V-shaped. Crew: 2 (+10 passengers).

The PVP, Small Protected Vehicle, is a French 4×4 wheeled light armored vehicle. It was developed in the 2000s. The PVP entered service in 2008. The PVP has level 2 protection. The PVP is employed by the French army and exported to Chile (15 units), Togo (6 units) and Romania (16 units). Versions: PVP – 3 doors / PVP – 5 doors / PVP HD – 5 doors, extended. Machine gun: 7.62mm. Crew: 2 + 3 to 5.

The Ural-63095 / Ural-63099 Typhoon-U is a Russian 6×6 wheeled multi-role armored vehicle. It was developed in the 2010s. The Typhoon-U entered service in 2014. The Typhoon-U is part of the MRAP type vehicles, Mine Resistant Ambush Protected. It has a V-shaped monocoque hull and is equipped with shock-absorbing seats. They are employed in the Southern Military District for troop transport, reconnaissance, as command post vehicle, as CBRN vehicle. The vehicle can receive a remotely operated turret equipped with light weapons. Machine gun: 12.7mm optional. Crew: 3 + 16 Ural-63095 / 2 + 12 Ural-63099.

The BMPT Terminator is a Russian heavy combat armored vehicle. It was developed in the 2000s-2010s. The BMPT entered service in 2011. The BMPT, Boyévaya Machina Podderjki Tankov – tank support combat vehicle, is intended for the fire support mission of tank units by destroying enemy anti-tank means. The BMPT Terminator uses the T-72 or T-90 battle tank chassis with the driver\'s position at the front center and the engine at the rear. The BMPT has a wide range of armament. The two-man turret on the superstructure is equipped with two 30mm 2A42 cannons, a 7.62mm PKT coaxial machine gun and four Ataka-T laser-guided supersonic anti-tank missiles. Two AG-17D automatic grenade launchers are installed at the front-left and front-right of the vehicle. The AG-17D are controlled, independently of the main armament, by two crew members installed on either side of the driver. Crew: 5.

The Boomerang is a project of the Russian 8×8 wheeled combat armored vehicle. It has been in development from the 2010s. The Boomerang is expected to enter service in 2019-2020. Versions: K-16 Boomerang – APC, armored personnel carrier / K-17 Boomerang – IFV, infantry fighting vehicle. K-16 Boomerang armament: Machine gun - 12.7mm. K-17 Boomerang armament: Machine gun - 30mm. Missile: 2×2 Kornet. Crew: 3 + 7 to 8.

The MT-LB is a Russian multi-role transport armored vehicle. It was developed in the Soviet Union in the 1960s. The MT-LB entered service in 1964. The MT-LB is designed as an artillery tractor and equipment transporter. Subsequently, the MT-LB was adopted as a troop transport version, medical evacuation vehicle and platform for installing different systems and equipment.

The VBCI, Infantry Fighting Vehicle, is a French 8×8 wheeled combat armored vehicle. It was developed in the 2000s. The VBCI entered service in 2008. The VBCI was developed to replace the tracked AMX-10P infantry fighting vehicle. The VBCI is put into service within French Army infantry units in 2008 in two versions: VBCI-VCI, Infantry Fighting Vehicle, and VBCI-VPC, Command Post Vehicle. The VBCI-VCI version is equipped with the single-man Tarask turret armed with the 25mm M811 dual-feed automatic cannon and the 7.62mm MAG 58 coaxial machine gun. It can be used by the vehicle commander in remote control function. The VBCI-VPC version is equipped with two SIR stations and is armed with a remotely operated 12.7mm machine gun. Crew: 3 + 8.

The BTR-4 is a Ukrainian 8×8 wheeled combat armored vehicle. It was developed in the 2000s. The BTR-4 entered service in 2011 in the Iraqi army and in 2014 in the Ukrainian army. The BTR-4 architecture differs from the lineage of the Soviet BTR-60/70/80 family. The BTR-4 is equipped with a remotely operated turret, armed with a 30mm cannon. Crew: 3 + 8.

The FV101 Scorpion is a British reconnaissance armored vehicle. It was developed in the 1960s. The FV101 Scorpion entered service in 1973. The FV101 Scorpion was developed as a reconnaissance vehicle. It is armed with the L23A1 76mm cannon and the L43A1 7.62mm coaxial machine gun. Scorpion left active service in the British army in 1994. Crew: 3.

MaxxPro is an armored military transport or recovery vehicle manufactured by the United States. It is an MRAP type vehicle with a V-shaped hull to protect against landmines. The MaxxPro is armed only with a roof turret that can accommodate a 7.62mm or 12.7mm machine gun but also other types of infantry weapons such as a TOW missile or a Mk19 automatic grenade launcher. Crew: 2 plus 8.

The SUPERAV is developed by Iveco and BAE Systems under the ACV, Amphibious Combat Vehicle program, for the United States Marine Corps. Cannon: up to 30mm. Machine gun: 12.7mm. Automatic grenade launcher: Mk19 40mm. Crew: 3 + 13.

The Ajax is a British combat armored vehicle. It was developed in the 2010s. The Ajax entered service in 2019. The Ajax is intended for reconnaissance and combat missions. The Ajax uses the tracked chassis of the ASCOD 2 armored vehicle. It is equipped with a turret armed with a 40mm CT40/40 CTAS cannon that uses telescoped ammunition and a 7.62mm L94A1 coaxial machine gun. The vehicle is equipped with a remotely operated turret. Crew: 2 + 4.

The VBHP, Highly Protected Armored Vehicle, Aravis is a French 4×4 wheeled armored vehicle. It was developed in the 2000s. The VBHP Aravis entered service in 2009. Cannon: 20mm. Coaxial machine gun: 7.62mm / 12.7mm. Crew: 2 + 5.

The BRM-3K Rys (Lynx in Russian) is a Russian reconnaissance armored vehicle. It was developed in the 1990s. The BRM-3K Rys entered service in 1995. The BRM-3K Rys is developed on the BMP-3 infantry fighting vehicle chassis for reconnaissance units. Its missions are: observation, target detection, position determination of detected targets and intelligence transmission to higher echelons. The BRM-3K is equipped with a 1RL-133-3 Doppler effect ground surveillance radar, a laser rangefinder, a thermal camera, a navigation system, a data transmission system at a distance of 100 km while moving and 350 km stationary. Cannon: 30mm. Crew: 3 + 3.

The BTR-D is a Russian armored personnel carrier for airborne units. It was developed in the Soviet Union in the early 1970s. The BTR-D entered service in 1974. The BTR-D is developed from the BMD-1 IFV chassis. It offers superior internal volume for installing different equipment and weapon systems. The BTR-D lacks a turret and can receive one or two 7.62mm machine guns. Amphibious. The BTR-D chassis was used for different armored vehicles. Machine gun: 7.62mm PKT. Crew: 3 + 10.
The Patria 6×6 is developed by the Finnish company. The vehicle can accommodate two crew members and ten infantrymen. The standard armament consists of a 12.7mm heavy machine gun.

The Cougar is an American MRAP type armored vehicle. It was developed in the 2000s. The Cougar entered service in 2002. The MRAP, Mine Resistant Ambush Protected, Cougar is designed to provide better protection to its crew against mines and explosive devices. The Cougar is developed in 4×4 and 6×6 versions. Machine gun: 12.7mm / 7.62mm. Crew: 2 + 4 Cougar 4×4 / 2 + 8 Cougar 6×6.

The Eitan is an Israeli 8×8 wheeled combat armored vehicle project. It is under development. The first demonstrator of the Eitan was unveiled by the Israeli Ministry of Defense on September 1, 2016. It is being developed to replace the fleet of M113 tracked armored personnel carriers. The Eitan can be declined in different versions: APC, wheeled IFV, command, medical evacuation, mortar carrier, engineer, etc. Armament: Machine gun: 12.7mm / 7.62mm. Crew: 3 + 9.

The ERC-90 is a French 6×6 wheeled Heavy Weapons Vehicle. It was developed in the 1970s. The ERC-90 entered service in 1979. The ERC-90 is mainly used in reconnaissance units. The ERC-90 has amphibious capability and is propelled in water with two propellers. Cannon: 90mm. Crew: 3.

The LPPV, Light Protection Patrol Vehicle, Foxhound is a British 4×4 wheeled armored vehicle. It was developed in the 2000s. The Foxhound entered service in 2011. Machine gun: 2 x 7.62mm. Crew: 2 + 4.

The FV107 Scimitar is a British reconnaissance armored vehicle. It was developed in the 1960s. The FV107 Scimitar entered service in 1971. The FV107 Scimitar was developed as a reconnaissance vehicle. It is equipped with a two-man turret armed with the 30mm L21 Rarden automatic cannon and a 7.62mm coaxial machine gun. Crew: 3.

The GRF is a Dutch Special Forces vehicle. It was developed in the 2010s. The GRF (Ground force) is a light tactical platform air-transportable, specially designed for Special Forces units. The GRF can receive different configurations and integrate a wide range of armaments and equipment. Armament: M2 Browning 12.7mm. / HK GMG 40mm automatic grenade launcher. Crew: 3 + 1.

The Higuard is a French MRAP type Higuard armored vehicle. It was developed in the 2010s. The Higuard entered service in 2012. The pronounced V-shaped hull offers a high level of protection against mines and IEDs. The vehicle carries two crew members and ten infantrymen. The Higuard can receive a remotely operated turret armed with a 12.7mm heavy machine gun, a 7.62mm machine gun or 40mm automatic grenade launcher.

The Lazar-3 is a Serbian 8×8 wheeled combat armored vehicle. It was developed in the 2010s. The Lazar-3 entered service in 2018. The vehicle has five windows on each side and two windows at the rear allowing a good level of observation. Each window has a firing port for light weapons. In its IFV version, infantry fighting vehicle, the Lazar-3 can receive a turret armed with a 20mm or 30mm automatic cannon. The APC version, armored personnel carrier, is equipped with a remotely operated turret armed with a 12.7mm heavy machine gun. Armament: 30mm. Crew: 3 + 9.

The LMV Lince is an Italian 4×4 wheeled multi-role armored vehicle. It was developed in the 1990s by Iveco. The LMV Lince entered service in 2001. The LMV, Light Multirole Vehicle, Lince (Lynx in Italian) is also called M65. It is designed for liaison, convoy escort and reconnaissance missions. Its armor protects against small caliber weapons. An additional armor kit offers protection against 12.7mm ammunition. The LMV Lince is widely exported worldwide. It is employed by the British army under the name Panther. Within the Russian army, it is employed under the name Rys, assembled under license by Kamaz. Crew: 1 + 4.

The SpPz Luchs is a German 8×8 wheeled reconnaissance armored vehicle. It was developed in the 1960s-1970s. The SpPz Luchs entered service in 1975. The SpPz, Spähpanzer, Luchs (Lynx) was developed for reconnaissance units. To optimize its mobility capability, it has an original architecture. The chassis has two driver positions installed at the front and rear. The vehicle can turn around and go in the opposite direction after being taken over by the rear driver. The SpPz Luchs is an amphibious vehicle, propelled in water with two propellers. The SpPz Luchs is equipped with a two-man turret, armed with the 20mm MK-20 Rh-202 cannon. In 1985, the Luchs A2 model receives a thermal camera. Within the German army, the Luchs is replaced by the Fennek 4×4 wheeled reconnaissance vehicle. Crew: 4.

The Pars III is a Turkish 8×8 wheeled combat armored vehicle. It was developed in the 2000s-2010s. The Pars III entered service in 2017. The Pars III, with a maximum weight of 30 tons, is equipped with a single-man Saber turret armed with the Orbital ATK M242 Bushmaster dual-feed automatic cannon and a 7.62mm coaxial machine gun. Its crew is three men and nine equipped infantrymen. Armament: 25mm. Crew: 3 + 9.

The LAV-25, Light Armoured Vehicle 25mm, is an American reconnaissance armored vehicle. It was developed in the 1970s-1980s. The LAV-25 entered service in 1983. The LAV-25 is employed within reconnaissance units. The LAV-25 is based on the 8×8 wheeled Piranha armored vehicle chassis. The LAV-25 is equipped with a two-man turret derived from the M2 Bradley infantry fighting vehicle. The armament consists of the 25mm M242 Bushmaster automatic cannon, a 7.62mm M240 coaxial machine gun. Crew: 3 + 6.

The Titus is a French 6×6 wheeled armored vehicle. It was developed in the 2010s by Nexter Systems. The vehicle can accommodate up to twelve infantrymen in addition to its crew of two to three men. The Titus has a high level of ballistic and mine protection. It can receive a remotely operated turret armed with a 20mm automatic cannon, a 12.7mm heavy machine gun or a 40mm automatic grenade launcher. Crew: 2-3 + 12.

The KamAZ-53949 Typhoon-K is a Russian 4×4 wheeled multi-role armored vehicle. It was developed in the 2010s. The Typhoon-K entered service in 2019. The 4×4 Typhoon-K is part of the MRAP type vehicles, Mine Resistant Ambush Protected. It has a V-shaped monocoque hull and is equipped with shock-absorbing seats. Armament: 12.7mm. Crew: 2 + 8.

The VBMR Griffon (Multi-Role Armored Vehicle) is a French 6×6 wheeled armored personnel carrier. It was developed by Nexter Systems. The VBMR Griffon entered service in 2019. Armament: 12.7mm / Automatic grenade launcher: 40mm. Crew: 2 + 8.

The VCR, Wheeled Combat Vehicle, is a French 6×6 wheeled combat armored vehicle. It was developed in the 1970s. The VCR entered service in 1979. The VCR is based on the 4×4 wheeled M3 vehicle. It has the same running gear and engine as the ERC-90 Sagaie heavy weapons vehicle. The VCR is produced in several versions. The main version is the VCR/TT, Troop Transport. It can receive a 7.62mm machine gun or a 12.7mm heavy machine gun. The specific versions are equipped with HOT missiles, Milan missiles or a 20mm cannon. Crew: 3 + 9.

GBC 180 - Gazelle Berliet Cargo (180 hp). It is mainly intended to transport personnel, freight or shelters and to perform specialized recovery (lot 7) and fuel supply (CCT) missions. All GBC 180 "torpedo cab platform with tarpaulin" are pre-equipped to receive a 12.7 ring mount. The GBC 180 is a 6 x 6 tactical vehicle, able to carry three people in the cab.

Light command and liaison vehicle, unarmored, the 4X4 tactical vehicle (VT4) is a militarized 4x4 type, intended to provide liaisons for 5 soldiers or 4 FELIN equipped combatants in an operational context (domestic operations like Sentinelle or external operations in stabilization and normalization phase) and operational preparation (activity safety, maneuvers, training). The VT4 is a versatile light tactical vehicle replacing the P4 vehicle (Peugeot 4 wheel drive). It combines modernity, power, crossing capacity and has a complete driving profile (on road, on tracks and off-road). Pre-equipped to receive the window protection grille kit Pre-equipped to receive two PR4G radios, a command system type tactical touch computer and a GPS Equipped with light source concealment systems (black-out). Empty weight (EW): 2.66 tons. Payload: 770 kg. Range: 800 km. Crew: 5 soldiers or 4 combatants with FELIN gear and equipment.

The Peugeot P4 is a light four-wheel drive vehicle produced by French automaker Peugeot from 1982 to 1992. Although equipped and powered by Peugeot, the P4 is a variant of the Mercedes-Benz G-Class built under license.

The Masstech T4 is a French light military vehicle, based on the Toyota Land Cruiser HZJ 76 and modified by the company Technamm. In particular, the vehicle is equipped with a PR4G radio, a SITEL terminal and a DAGR GPS. It can carry four equipped combatants or five passengers. Deployed only in France with Operation Sentinelle, its engine, rustic and compatible with African and military fuels, authorizes its deployment in OPEX.
The Renault TRM 2000 is a French 4 wheel drive military truck (attested by its initials: Toutes Roues Motrices) designed for support missions in difficult terrain. It was produced from 1982 to 1990.

The VAB, Forward Armored Vehicle, is a French wheeled armored personnel carrier. The VAB entered service in 1976. The VAB is developed in 4×4 and 6×6 configurations. The VAB engine is installed behind the driver\'s position. A wide range of armored vehicles is developed on the VAB chassis. Among the main versions are the VAB PC Command post, VAB T20-13 with a 20mm cannon, VAB Mephisto with four HOT anti-tank missiles, VAB Engineer, VAB Medical, VAB CBRN Reconnaissance, VAB RASIT with a ground surveillance radar. Machine gun: 12.7mm. Crew: 2 + 10. Engine: V6 diesel, 220 hp.

It was a very light four-wheeled reconnaissance vehicle, Brazilian army. In the 1970s and 1980s, the Brazilian army bought about 1,300 armored vehicles from Engesa, and 2,000 more vehicles were exported to other countries, especially to Arab states and in Africa in general (Libya, Tunisia and Iraq being the largest buyers). Crew: 3. Armament: 12.7mm machine gun.

The Ural-4320 is an all-terrain military truck produced by Ural Automotive Plant since 1976. This vehicle was designed to meet the Soviet army\'s needs for transporting troops and equipment in difficult conditions, such as rough terrain or extreme environments.

The BMD-1 is a Russian infantry fighting vehicle for airborne units. It was developed in the Soviet Union in the early 1960s. The BMD-1 entered service in 1969. The single-man turret is armed with a 73mm 2A28 Grom cannon, a 7.62mm PKT coaxial machine gun. Crew: 2 + 5.

The BMD-2 is a Russian infantry fighting vehicle for airborne units. It was developed in the Soviet Union in the early 1980s. The BMD-2 is developed from the BMD-1 chassis. It has the new weapon system with a single-man turret armed with the 30mm 2A42 cannon and a 7.62mm PKT coaxial machine gun. For anti-tank combat, it is equipped with a system capable of firing 9M111 Fagot AT-4 or 9M113 Konkurs AT-5 anti-tank missiles. Crew: 2 + 5.

The BMD-3 is a Russian infantry fighting vehicle for airborne units. It was developed in the Soviet Union in the 1980s. The BMD-3 entered service in 1990. In the 1980s, the USSR sought to develop a new air-droppable infantry fighting vehicle to replace the BMD-1 and BMD-2 family. The BMD-3 is air-droppable. Cannon: 30mm 2A42 x100.2 calibers. Coaxial machine gun: 7.62mm PKT. Automatic hood grenade launcher: 30mm AG-17. Crew: 2 + 5.

The BMD-4 is a Russian infantry fighting vehicle for airborne units. It was developed in the early 2000s. The BMD-4 entered service in 2004 in limited quantities. The BMD-4 has the same five-road-wheel chassis as its predecessor the BMD-3. The vehicle receives a new Bakhtcha-U turret which significantly increases firepower. The Bakhtcha-U turret is derived from the BMP-3 weapon system. It is equipped with a 100mm 2A70 cannon, a 30mm 2A72 automatic cannon and a 7.62mm PKT coaxial machine gun. The BMD-4 is air-droppable and optimized for airborne operations. Crew: 2 + 5.

The ZBD-05 is a Chinese amphibious infantry fighting vehicle. It was developed in the 2000s. The ZBD-05 entered service in 2005. The ZBD-05 is developed specifically for marine infantry units. The vehicle was unveiled in 2006 under the designation ZBD-2000. To improve its amphibious qualities, the ZBD-05 is equipped with a large front plow blade. The ZBD-05 is equipped with a two-man turret armed with the 30mm ZPT-99 automatic cannon, a 7.62mm coaxial machine gun and HJ-73C anti-tank missiles. The vehicle accommodates three crew members and nine equipped infantrymen. Several vehicles are developed on the ZTD-05 chassis.
